thread:
julie_support: Hi team — customer nina_customer reports a ~20k credit drop overnight. They think embeddings jobs retried a lot. Account: acct_9b2f, project: app-team-prod. Promo code 'FREE60' was supposed to apply but balance still depleted. Can we triage?

nina_customer: yes, we woke up to a 19.6k credit reduction. We run nightly bulk embeddings at 00:05 UTC. It looked like the job fired twice? Attached screenshots in original ticket.

julie_support: thanks. asking for logs and request IDs. nina, can you paste a couple of sample request ids from the job run?

nina_customer: here — request ids: r_20240720_00_01_7f2, r_20240720_00_01_9c3, r_20240720_00_02_a11. Each corresponds to an embeddings call to /v1/embeddings.

sam_sre: :eyes: quick hypothesis — worker restarted during the batch and retried without preserving idempotency-key. If the background job doesn't set idempotency-key on each embedding request, our retry logic will reconsume credits. Can we get the worker command?

pete_dev: the nightly job is a Celery chain in our infra. Here's the relevant chunk of the task runner: 

```
celery.task(bind=True, max_retries=3)
def emit_batch(self, batch):
    for item in batch:
        # we used to send sync, now we fire async
        client.embeddings.create(model="open-embed-1", input=item.text)
```

No idempotency headers were set — ooops. We thought retries were handled by Celery, not API.

marlene_billing: noted. if API calls were duplicated we'll need to credit back. julie, can you collect earliest/last timestamps and total tokens for the three example requests? billing will need approximate token counts to compute a credit refund.

julie_support: collecting now from logs. For r_20240720_00_01_7f2: tokens=12, r_...9c3: tokens=11, r_...a11: tokens=9. But the job shows ~48k embeddings requests in the window 00:05–00:20 UTC and three bursts of retries. The weird bit: our logs show the service returned 202 for some requests and then the client retried.

sam_sre: can you paste the service-side logs for one of the request ids? look for our retry_count/inflight markers and the X-Idempotency-Key header presence/absence.

julie_support: copied snippet from proxy logs for r_20240720_00_01_7f2:

```
[2024-07-20T00:05:12Z] proxy-inbound id=r_20240720_00_01_7f2 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=202 user=acct_9b2f
[2024-07-20T00:05:12Z] proxy-inbound id=r_20240720_00_01_7f2 headers={"Content-Length":"128","Authorization":"Bearer sk-***","X-Request-Id":"r_20240720_00_01_7f2"}
[2024-07-20T00:05:13Z] backend-upstream id=r_20240720_00_01_7f2 status=200 worker=pool-7 call_id=call_883
```
No X-Idempotency-Key set.

pete_dev: doh. Celery retried the task after a transient DB lock at 00:06, and the retry path re-emitted the whole batch without dedupe. That explains duplicate sends. We need to patch to set an idempotency key per document id and persist it in the task context.

marlene_billing: from billing side — we'll provisionally credit the net duplicate cost once engineering confirms duplicate counts. Please provide a sanitized count of duplicated embeddings (not token-level yet) so we can approximate.

nina_customer: rough numbers: same job run has ~48k unique items, but our diff shows ~96k embedding calls during that window — looks like ~48k duplicates.

sam_sre: can we verify if any retries were triggered by transient 5xx from our upstream? If the service returned 2xx but the client retried, that's client-side double-send. The proxy snippet shows 202 then backend 200. Suggest we also grep for 503/504 around 00:05–00:10 to ensure some tasks retried due to upstream failures.

julie_support: grep done — small cluster of 503s at 00:06:05 from one shard (node-gpu-4) for ~45s. So mix of transient upstream errors + client-side retry logic without idempotency caused replays.

pete_dev: plan: (1) immediate patch to worker to include header X-Idempotency-Key: <project>-<doc-id>-<job-run-ts>, (2) add dedupe check before emit_batch, (3) request billing credit for estimated cost of duplicates. I'll open a PR and candidate hotfix today.

marlene_billing: once engineering confirms duplicated_count and token_estimate send to billing@redwood.com with account id and promo code. We'll start a provisional credit for the duplicate charge and finalize after invoice reconciliation.

julie_support: nina — we'll coordinate the credit and keep you posted. Sorry for the trouble.

nina_customer: thanks for the quick triage. One ask: can you also check promo grant application? the promo showed as consumed in their portal but code was attached to account earlier.

julie_support: promo note: promo 'FREE60' granted in account creation flow on 2024-07-01 but a downstream sync bug sometimes failed to attach promo to scheduled-job namespace, so jobs charged full. We'll treat that as two issues: duplicate sends + promo not applied for background jobs.

sam_sre: flagged a task for infra: ensure promo metadata is included in background-job credentials (ticket INF-3219).

pete_dev: PR created — hotfix route to add idempotency header and add safe-emit check. link: https://git.internal/redwood/app-team-prod/pulls/472

deploy-bot: deploy requested by pete_dev for hotfix branch at 2024-07-20T09:18:00Z — status: scheduled to staging.

julie_support: closing loop — billing will provision provisional credit, dev to hotfix and deploy, infra to ensure promo metadata flows to scheduler. I'll update ticket with final amounts once billing confirms. :white_check_mark:
